subject: Scaling window: incremental uplift, co-term glidepath, and usage cushion
messages:
From: Elena Cruz <elena@orchidai.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Orchid AI Procurement <procurement@orchidai.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Scaling window: incremental uplift, co-term glidepath, and usage cushion

Hi Mateo,

Hope you’re well. We’re seeing a predictable surge in inference consumption for our image-labeling pipelines starting in July; projection attached. We’re exploring options for a mid-contract uplift rather than a step-change commitment. Two asks: 1) can you outline a staged uplift that lets us opt into additional capacity (burst lanes) with quarterly invoicing, and 2) can we co-term the additional capacity to our existing renewal on 2027-10-01?

High level numbers: expected uplift ~40% of current committed tokens during Q3, tapering to ~20% by Q4. We’d like a cushion (soft buffer) so brief spikes don’t throttle production.

Attached: orchid_usage_report_q1.csv (summary).

Thanks — can we get a short proposal this week so procurement can start internal review?

Best,
Elena Cruz
Head of ML Ops
Orchid AI

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena@orchidai.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scaling window: incremental uplift, co-term glidepath, and usage cushion

Elena — thanks for the context and the Q1 report. This is manageable, and we have a couple approaches that match what you described. Quick clarifying q’s before we draft a formal amendment: 

- When you say "burst lanes," do you expect guaranteed headroom (reserved GPUs) or short-lived burst (best-effort) behind a higher rate?
- Is the 40% increase sustained or driven by distributed/seasonal jobs (e.g., nightly batches)?
- Any procurement constraints on invoice cadence (quarterly vs monthly) or PO timing?

High-level options I’m thinking we can propose (short bullets):
1) Staged reserved uplifts — two tranches (Jul 1 & Sep 1) with incremental reserved capacity, co-term to 2027-10-01, quarterly invoicing for uplift.
2) Burst cushion + on-demand — keep current reserved commit, add soft buffer (10-15%) that is billed at a blended burst rate and caps monthly overages; co-term only for reserved uplift.
3) Hybrid — small reserved tranche + burst cushion; discounted uplift bands if run-rate stays above thresholds for 60 days.

If you can confirm the answers above I’ll draft option 1 with concrete numbers and a recommended discount ladder.

Thanks —
Mateo Alvarez
Account Lead, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Cruz <elena@orchidai.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scaling window: incremental uplift, co-term glidepath, and usage cushion

Thanks Mateo. Answers inline: 
- We prefer guaranteed headroom for the critical nightly pipelines — so reserved GPUs for the first tranche, with the ability to dial down if not needed later.
- The 40% is mostly nightly batch jobs for a new labeling workflow; expect steady across Jul-Aug then a taper in Sep-Oct (hence co-term preference).
- Procurement prefers quarterly invoicing but can accept one-upfront PO if it speeds implementation.

If you can put an illustration of the discount bands and the invoicing cadence (quarterly vs one PO) that’ll help our CFO sign off. Also include a sample amendment to the order (draft) so legal can eyeball.

- Elena

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena@orchidai.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Orchid AI Procurement <procurement@orchidai.com>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Scaling window: incremental uplift, co-term glidepath, and usage cushion

Team — looping you in to propose a clean path. Below is a concise proposal (attached as draft_amendment_v1.pdf):

Proposal (summary):
- Tranche A (go-live 2027-07-01): 25% reserved capacity increase (guaranteed), quarterly invoicing for this uplift.
- Tranche B (go-live 2027-09-01): optional 15% reserved increase if sustained run-rate > 30% uplift for 30 days. If triggered, Tranche B is co-termed to 2027-10-01.
- Burst cushion: additional 10% soft buffer billed at blended burst rate (1.6x hosted rate) to absorb spikes; automatic runback if not used for 45 days.
- Discount ladder (applies to reserved uplift only): 7% discount for Aug+Sep run-rate > 30% of baseline; 12% discount if > 40% for 60 consecutive days.
- Invoicing: default quarterly invoices for uplift; procurement option for single upfront PO covering Jul–Sep with a credit applied for unused capacity at co-term.

Attachments: draft_amendment_v1.pdf (draft amendment with legal-friendly language), orchid_usage_report_q1.csv (from Elena).

Tessa — can you confirm standard SLAs for reserved tranches and confirm if the burst blended rate above aligns with current pricing constructs? Ben — finance, can you flag billing/credit mechanics if they choose the upfront PO option?

Thanks —
Mateo

> - The 40% is mostly nightly batch jobs for a new labeling workflow; expect steady across Jul-Aug then a taper in Sep-Oct (hence co-term preference).
> - Procurement prefers quarterly invoicing but can accept one-upfront PO if it speeds implementation.
>
> If you can put an illustration of the discount bands and the invoicing cadence (quarterly vs one PO) that’ll help our CFO sign off. Also include a sample amendment to the order (draft) so legal can eyeball.
>
> - Elena

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Cruz <elena@orchidai.com>, Orchid AI Procurement <procurement@orchidai.com>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Scaling window: incremental uplift, co-term glidepath, and usage cushion

Mateo / Tessa — reviewed the draft. Finance is comfortable with the structure with the following notes: 

- Approve discount ladder as-is, but discounts apply only to reserved commit line item (not to burst).
- If Orchid elects the single upfront PO for Jul–Sep: we can offer a 1.5% additional credit on unused reserved capacity at co-term instead of cash refund; credit is applied to the Oct invoice run.
- Billing mechanics: quarterly invoices preferred. For the upfront PO we’ll issue a proforma invoice and then reconciled credit.
- Need to add explicit language on proration if they reduce reserved capacity mid-tranche (standard 30-day notice, prorated credit for remaining full months).

I’ve flagged accounting constraints and added the phrasing to the attached amendment.

-ben
Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena@orchidai.com>, Orchid AI Procurement <procurement@orchidai.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scaling window: incremental uplift, co-term glidepath, and usage cushion

Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround and procurement clarity. Next steps: 

1) I’ve attached draft_amendment_v1.pdf with Ben’s billing language and Tessa’s SLA bullets. Please review the single-page summary (page 1) for the Jul/Sept tranches and confirm whether Orchid prefers quarterly invoicing or the upfront PO.
2) If green, I’ll open a DocuSign envelope for the amendment (link below) and schedule a short 30-minute kickoff to align implementation timeline with your infra team (target go-live 2027-07-01 for Tranche A).

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/DEAL-8473-amend
Meeting: I’ll propose 2027-05-05 10:00 AM PT unless you prefer another slot.

Appreciate the quick collaboration — will follow up with the e-sign envelope once you confirm invoicing preference.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Lead, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference
